newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse gets new second-tier listing.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse gets new second-tier listing.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Wednesday another company had joined in trading on its second tier, bringing to 46 the total number of listings.
"Shares of Silcotub started being traded at Wednesday's session," a bourse official said.

Silcotub, based in Zalau, in the Transylvanian region, is a state-run steel prefabs and pipes maker. Its share capital is of around 116.5 billion lei, in shares with a nominal value of 25,000 lei each.
The State Ownership Fund is the company's majority stockholder, with a 69.99 percent stake. An investment company holds 16.33 percent and individual shareholders have the rest.
A Silcotub statement showed it had had a net profit of some 6.6 billion lei last year, up from around two billion in 1995.
Silcotub's future plans include reducing production costs, investing up to 30 million marks in upgrading and penetrating fresh markets.
The Bucharest stock exchange trades eight companies on its first tier.
